p|categorias_que|rastreador: A public list recognizes it as tracking: it is used to follow you from one site to the next.
p|categorias_que|publicidad: It is on the advertising lists: it shows you ads, or measures them.
p|categorias_que|telemetria: Usage data a program sends back to its maker.
p|categorias_que|esperado: What a computer needs to work: system updates, certificates, the system’s own security and connectivity checks, time, recognized messaging and video calls, and what GUARDIANA needs for its license.
p|categorias_que|desconocido: No open tracking list knows it. It does not mean it is suspicious.
p|categorias_que|red_local: Devices in your home finding each other. It does not go out to the internet.
p|categorias_que|entrega: A network that carries other companies’ content. Not the destination: the road.
p|categorias_que|de_empresa: Its owner is known (the next column names the company) and no list marks it as tracking or advertising, but the name does not say what it is for. A label, never a verdict.
p|categorias_que|pista_anuncios: No list has it yet, but the name carries a technical term from ad auctions (prebid, rtb, ssp, dsp, cookie syncing). The name says so; it is not a verdict.
p|categorias_que|pista_pago: A payment or a subscription at that company: the name carries “checkout”, “pay”, “billing” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
p|categorias_que|pista_cuenta: Signing in or your account data at that company: the name carries “login”, “accounts”, “auth” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
p|categorias_que|pista_medicion: Counts what you do in its app or site, for the company itself: the name carries “analytics”, “metrics”, “events”, “pixel” or similar. No public list marks it as tracking; the name says so.
p|categorias_que|pista_notificaciones: The notifications that reach your device: the name carries “push”, “notifications” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
p|categorias_que|pista_actualizaciones: Downloading updates or the installer: the name carries “update”, “download”, “release” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
p|categorias_que|pista_seguridad: Security checks of the browser or the system: the name carries “safebrowsing”, “smartscreen”, “captcha” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
p|categorias_que|pista_correo: Your email: the name carries “mail”, “smtp” or “imap”. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
p|categorias_que|pista_mensajes: Chat or messaging of that company: the name carries “chat”, “messages” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
p|categorias_que|pista_sincronizacion: Syncs or keeps a copy in the cloud: the name carries “drive” or “backup”. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
p|categorias_que|pista_contenido: Images, video, files or fonts the page needs to display: the name carries “cdn”, “static”, “img”, “media” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
p|categorias_que|pista_configuracion: The program asks for its settings or checks options: the name carries “config”, “settings”, “flags” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
p|categorias_que|pista_app: The program or app talking to its own company’s server in order to work: the name carries “api”, “gateway”, “backend” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
p|categorias_que|pista_web: That company’s site or app, the one you opened: the name is its domain or starts with “www”. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
p|categorias_que|sector: A {sector} website: what it does, from our open list of sectors. It says what it is, not whether to trust it.
p|senales|baliza: Contacts the same destination every {n} minutes, like a heartbeat.
p|senales|destino_nuevo: This device had never looked up this service before.
p|senales|fuera_de_horas: Talks at hours when this device usually does not.
p|senales|evasion_dns: Tries to resolve names on its own, out of GUARDIANA’s sight.
p|senales|volumen: Is asking far more than usual.
p|cli|certificado.periodo_malo: Invalid period. Use --mes YYYY-MM, or --desde YYYY-MM-DD --hasta YYYY-MM-DD (nothing: the last whole month).
p|cli|certificado.hecho: Flow certificate made: {ruta} (with its .sha256 and its .html beside it). {n} companies. SHA-256 seal: {sello}
p|cli|certificado.verificar.coincide: The certificate matches: rebuilt from this computer's record, it says exactly the same.
p|cli|certificado.verificar.otra_clasifi: The record's rows are the same, but the figures do not match. It was made by GUARDIANA {version} (this is {ahora}), which may have assigned some names to other companies.
p|cli|certificado.verificar.recortadas: The rows of that period have since been pruned from the record (retention period): it cannot be rebuilt, only its seal checked.
p|cli|certificado.verificar.no_coincide: The certificate does NOT match this computer's record: it comes from another computer, the file was changed, or rows of the record were changed.
p|cli|certificado.verificar.formato: This is not a GUARDIANA flow certificate (unknown format).
p|cli|certificado.verificar.ilegible: The file cannot be read as a flow certificate.
p|cli|certificado.verificar.sello: SHA-256 seal of the file: {sello} (compare it with its .sha256).
p|cli|certificado.verificar.cadena_mal: Warning: the hash chain of this computer's record does not fully verify right now (guardiana ledger --check).
p|cli|observe.arrancando: GUARDIANA is watching. Name → category → device. Ctrl+C to stop.
p|cli|observe.sin_privilegios: Listening on port 53 needs administrator rights (sudo).
p|cli|observe.limite_mac: On macOS, changing the system DNS needs administrator rights: the GUARDIANA desktop app asks for them and the panel makes the change.
p|cli|ledger.ok_recortado: Chain verified: {n} events correct; {p} earlier ones already summarized by retention.
p|cli|ledger.fallo: The chain is broken at event {id}: {motivo}.
p|cli|ledger.fallo.enlace: does not link to the previous event
p|cli|ledger.fallo.alterado: its data does not match its hash
p|cli|ledger.fallo.recortado: the most recent events are missing from here on
p|cli|ledger.fallo.sin_cabeza: the record of where the chain ends is missing, so there is no telling whether the latest events were removed
p|cli|dns.deshacer_pendiente: The change failed half-way and could not be fully undone. The copy of your previous setting is still saved: run guardiana dns --restore to put it back.
p|cli|observe.no_comparte: Queries from {dispositivo} are recorded but not shown here: its owner does not share the detail with the home panel.
p|cli|observe.vuelve_licencia: The license is valid again: GUARDIANA is this computer’s DNS again and is watching.
p|cli|observe.vuelve_licencia_sin_dns: The license is valid again: GUARDIANA is watching again.
p|cli|observe.vuelve_hogar: Home Mode is on again, as you had it.
p|cli|observe.relevo: Home Mode: the router still sends the home’s queries here. While GUARDIANA stands aside it only passes them on to {upstream} from {addr}, without looking at them or writing them down, so nobody is left without internet. Put the router’s DNS back as it was (or to automatic) when you can.
p|cli|observe.relevo_sin_arriba: Home Mode: I cannot find where to pass the home’s queries on, so I cannot relay them. If the router still sends the home’s queries here, put its DNS back as it was (or to automatic) now: without that, the phones and the rest are left without internet.
p|cli|observe.relevo_error: Home Mode: I cannot listen on the network to pass the home’s queries on ({error}). If the router still sends the home’s queries here, put its DNS back as it was (or to automatic) now.
p|cli|observe.upstream_propio: The DNS the network hands out is this very computer (the router gives out its address, as Home Mode asks), and GUARDIANA cannot ask itself: it asks {servers}.
p|cli|observe.solo_propio: The only DNS this computer knows is itself (the router gives out its address, as Home Mode asks), and GUARDIANA cannot ask itself. Set a fixed DNS on this computer (the router’s or your provider’s) or give one with --upstream IP.
p|cli|ledger.wipe.confirmar: This deletes the whole ledger, the devices, the rules and the record of connections. Type DELETE to confirm:
p|cli|ledger.wipe.hecho: Ledger deleted. GUARDIANA starts from zero.
p|cli|uso:
Usage:
  guardiana observe [--listen IP:PORT] [--upstream IP[:PORT]]... [--db PATH] [--canary] [--open] [--no-panel] [--panel-listen IP:PORT]
  guardiana ledger [--check | --wipe | --self | --last N] [--db PATH]
  guardiana export [--csv | --json] [--out FILE] [--device ID] [--category C] [--signal S] [--verdict V] [--limit N] [--db PATH]
  guardiana dns [--status | --apply --yes | --restore] [--db PATH]
  guardiana licencia [clave KEY | comprobar]
  guardiana trampa [crear | lista | quitar ID]   (trap files: a name that only exists inside)
  guardiana apps [--seconds N] [--crudo]   (Windows: which program asks for each name, watch only)
  guardiana verify [--json] [--certificado FILE.json]
  guardiana certificado [--mes YYYY-MM | --desde YYYY-MM-DD --hasta YYYY-MM-DD] [--dominios] [--empresa NAME] [--out FOLDER]   (flow certificate)
  guardiana reglas [deshacer ID | deshacer-hoy]
  guardiana informe               (weekly home report)
  guardiana hogar [status | on | off]
  guardiana service [install | uninstall | start | stop | status]
  guardiana panel                (opens the panel in the browser)
  guardiana comunicaciones       (Communications, chat and calls, in your browser; Linux and Mac)
  guardiana menu [--choice N]     (interactive test menu)
  guardiana version
p|cli|observe.upstream_auto: Upstream resolver taken from the system ({fuente}).
p|cli|observe.sin_upstream: Cannot find the system resolver. Give one with --upstream IP.
p|cli|observe.bucle: The upstream resolver cannot be the same address GUARDIANA listens on.
p|cli|observe.parado: GUARDIANA has stopped watching. {n} queries recorded in this session.
p|cli|observe.parado_uno: GUARDIANA has stopped watching. 1 query recorded in this session.
p|cli|observe.clave_dev: Notice: this binary carries the development key, not the release key.
p|cli|ledger.sin_extracto: No ledger yet at {ruta}. Run guardiana observe first.
p|cli|ledger.cabecera: time (UTC)  name  →  category  →  device  ·  state  ·  signals
p|cli|ledger.self.vacio: GUARDIANA has sent nothing out of this computer.
p|cli|ledger.self.cabecera: Connections GUARDIANA made by itself (all started by you):
p|cli|dns.estado.sin_resolutor: Cannot find any resolver configured on the system.
p|cli|dns.estado.aplicado: GUARDIANA has been the system DNS since {fecha}. A copy of the previous setting is saved.
p|cli|dns.estado.no_aplicado: GUARDIANA has not changed the system DNS.
p|cli|dns.consentimiento: This changes this computer’s DNS so that its queries go through GUARDIANA (127.0.0.1). An exact copy of the previous setting is saved and put back as it was with guardiana dns --restore.
p|cli|dns.aplicado: Done. This computer now resolves through GUARDIANA (127.0.0.1). It used to resolve with: {originales}. Undo: guardiana dns --restore.
p|cli|dns.ya_aplicado: GUARDIANA is already set as the DNS. To go back: guardiana dns --restore.
p|cli|dns.restaurado: System DNS restored exactly as it was.
p|cli|dns.no_hay_copia: There is no change by GUARDIANA to undo.
p|cli|dns.sin_admin: Changing the system DNS needs administrator rights. On Windows, open the terminal with “Run as administrator”; on a Mac, type the command with sudo in front.
p|cli|dns.aparcada_borrada: GUARDIANA had already given the DNS back as it was when it stood aside. Noted: when it watches again, it will not change it.
p|cli|dns.no_soportado: Changing the system DNS is only available on Windows and, with administrator rights, macOS.
p|cli|observe.upstream_copia: Upstream resolver taken from the copy saved before the DNS was changed: {servers}.
p|cli|observe.panel_nota: That link carries the key of your session; do not share it. Without it the panel shows nothing.
p|cli|observe.panel_error: The panel could not start: {error}. GUARDIANA keeps watching without a panel.
p|cli|observe.retencion: Everything is kept while the program is active. Nothing is deleted on its own.
p|cli|menu.opciones:
1  Watch in test mode (changes nothing) and open the panel
  2  See the ledger
  3  Watch for real: change this computer’s DNS, with your permission
  4  Undo the DNS change
  5  DNS status
  6  Home Mode: turn on
  7  Home Mode: turn off
  8  Home Mode: status
  9  Service: install (GUARDIANA starts with Windows and watches without a window)
 10  Service: remove
 11  Open the panel in the browser
 12  Service: status
 13  Verify: hash, signature, DNS, ports, lists (guardiana verify)
 14  License: status
  0  Exit
p|cli|menu.elige: Choose a number and press Enter:
p|cli|menu.no_entiendo: I did not understand the option. Type only the number.
p|cli|menu.volver: Press Enter to go back to the menu.
p|cli|menu.admin_necesario: This option changes system settings and needs administrator permission. Windows will ask you in a new window; press Yes.
p|cli|menu.admin_lanzado: Another window opened with administrator rights. Continue there; this one can stay open.
p|cli|menu.admin_fallo: Could not ask for administrator permission. Close this, right-click guardiana.exe and choose “Run as administrator”.
p|cli|menu.self_test: Sending six test questions to GUARDIANA…
p|cli|menu.self_test_hecho: Test questions sent. They should show above and in the panel.
p|cli|menu.parar: To stop and go back to the menu: press Ctrl+C.
p|cli|menu.confirmar_si: Type YES (in capitals) and press Enter to accept, or anything else to change nothing:
p|cli|menu.ya_servicio: GUARDIANA is already installed as a service and watches this computer without a window: this option is not needed and changes nothing. To see it, open the panel (option 11).
p|cli|menu.navega: GUARDIANA now watches everything this computer does. Open the browser, visit a couple of websites, and look here and in the panel.
p|cli|hogar.estado.on: Home Mode: on since {fecha}. Local network IP: {ip}.
p|cli|hogar.estado.off: Home Mode: off. No port open toward the network.
p|cli|hogar.estado.fuera: Home Mode: on since {fecha}, but paused: this computer is not on the network where you switched it on. It comes back by itself at home; if you moved or changed routers, “guardiana hogar on” as administrator takes this network as home.
p|cli|hogar.estado.aparcado: Home Mode: set aside, because GUARDIANA stands aside (the trial or the subscription ended). The router still sends the home’s queries here and GUARDIANA only passes them on, without looking. It comes back on by itself with the license; “guardiana hogar off” switches it off completely.
p|cli|hogar.on.hecho: Home Mode on. IP {ip}. GUARDIANA opens the ports on the local network in under a minute.
p|cli|hogar.off.hecho: Home Mode off. In under a minute GUARDIANA will listen only on this PC.
p|cli|hogar.qr: Phones scan the QR in the panel, Home Mode page: {url}
p|cli|observe.hogar: Home Mode: also listening on {addr} (DNS) and {panel} (panel). Firefox canary on.
p|cli|observe.hogar_no_privada: Home Mode requested, but the address {ip} is not on a private network. Nothing is opened outwards.
p|cli|observe.hogar_otra_red: Home Mode paused: this computer is not on the network where you switched it on. Away from home it opens no port toward the network; it comes back by itself when you are home again.
p|cli|observe.hueco: GUARDIANA was not watching between {desde} and {hasta}. It is on record.
p|cli|servicio.instalado: Service installed. GUARDIANA will start with the system and is already running. Panel: option 11 of the menu or guardiana panel.
p|cli|servicio.quitado: Service removed. GUARDIANA no longer starts with the system.
p|cli|apps.escuchando: Listening for {s} seconds to what Windows says about its own queries. Nothing is stored and nothing is blocked: this only looks.
p|cli|ia_programa_titulo: The program that made those queries, according to Windows itself. Only on this computer: from a phone in Home Mode you see the service name and nothing else.
p|cli|trampa_frase: This name only exists inside one of your trap files. GUARDIANA did not open that file or any other: all it saw is that something asked for this name, and that name cannot be known without having read the file.
p|cli|trampa.uso: I do not know “{cmd}”. Try: guardiana trampa crear | lista | quitar <id>
p|cli|trampa.creada:
Trap placed at {archivo}
If any program reads that file and looks up {nombre}, it will be written in the ledger with the time and, on Windows, with the program’s name.
p|cli|trampa.falta_id: Which one? guardiana trampa quitar <id>. The list is in: guardiana trampa lista
p|cli|trampa.no_esta: There is no trap with the id {id}.
